svg.text: HEAT BANKED IN ROCK · SECTION · CHARGE & DISCHARGE · VOLUME III · SHEET 1 OF 5

g.text: LOOSE REGOLITH JACKET — INSULATES, COSTS NOTHING
~1 m DOWN, THE MONTHLY SWING IS ALREADY GONE
FIG. B — REGOLITH IS A BLANKET
NO AIR BETWEEN GRAINS → ALMOST NO CONDUCTION (Langseth et al., 1976)
DETAIL A — ONE MATERIAL, TWO STATES
SUPPLYING HEAT: SUPERB — keep water liquid, crops alive, bearings working.
SUPPLYING ELECTRICITY: MEDIOCRE — any heat engine is capped by the
temperature difference, so most stored energy is rejected, not converted.
IT DOES NOT REPLACE ELECTRICAL STORAGE. IT REMOVES THE BIGGEST LOAD
FROM IT — BECAUSE A SETTLEMENT'S FIRST NEED AT NIGHT IS NOT TO FREEZE.
ENERGY = MASS × SPECIFIC HEAT × TEMPERATURE CHANGE.
ROCK IS NOT DENSE STORAGE — CAPACITY IS BOUGHT IN TONNES.
THE MASS IS FREE. THE SINTERING ENERGY IS NOT — RECOVER IT OVER MANY CYCLES.

svg.text: DESIGNED BY: W.A. SANDUN PRIYANKARA WIJERATHNE · sandunwijerathne51@gmail.com · github.com/sandunwijerathne

g.text: 1 — DAY CHARGE: concentrator, surplus electricity, or waste heat
2 — LOOSE JACKET: regolith as found — the insulation is free
3 — DENSE CORE: sintered or cast regolith — the storage (DETAIL A)
4 — EMBEDDED HEAT PIPES: the engineering crux
5 — NIGHT DRAW-DOWN to habitat heat loads
